items.title: kube-apiserver: request can hang for 40–90s when its etcd transport is recycled mid-flight (grpc-go v1.72.2 bug, fixed in v1.77.0; affects release-1.34/1.35)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

items.body:
### What happened?

In our CI environment (Calico Felix functional tests, which start a fresh kube-apiserver per test), a LIST of a CRD hung inside the apiserver for 13+ seconds while identical LISTs from other clients, through the same apiserver, succeeded within 300 ms. The stuck request was still blocked on its first attempt of an etcd KV/Range RPC when the client gave up:

```
{"level":"warn","logger":"etcd-client","caller":"v3@v3.6.5/retry_interceptor.go:65","msg":"retrying of unary invoker failed","target":"etcd-endpoints://0xc004ab9680/[...]:2379","method":"/etcdserverpb.KV/Range","attempt":0,"error":"rpc error: code = Canceled desc = context canceled"}
E ... timeout.go:140] "Post-timeout activity" ... method="GET" path="/apis/crd.projectcalico.org/v1/globalnetworksets"
```

etcd (single node, v3.5.24) was healthy throughout: no slow-apply or read-index warnings, and it served all other requests, including the same LIST from other clients, in milliseconds.

The hung request was the first request ever for that CRD on the freshly started apiserver. First requests trigger lazy creation of the CRD's storage, including a new etcd client (one per CRD - #111476). The hang coincided with a burst of transport churn from ~14 CRD storages being created at once:

```
W ... grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect ... Err: connection error: desc = "error reading server preface: read tcp [...]: use of closed network connection"
W ... grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect ... Err: "transport: failed to write client preface: write tcp [...]: use of closed network connection"
W ... grpc: addrConn.createTransport failed to connect ... Err: "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp [...]: operation was canceled"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

All requests for that list serviced promptly.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Repeatedly hammer the list CR path on freshly started API server.  It is probabilistic and infrequent.

### Anything else we need to know?

Upstream fix (assuming RCA below is correct)

- grpc/grpc-go#8425 ("Transport close blocks on unresponsive reader"), fixed by grpc/grpc-go#8534 ("transport: Invoke net.Conn.SetReadDeadline in http2_client.Close"), released in grpc-go v1.77.0. Related hardening: grpc/grpc-go#8615 (pickfirstleaf stuck in IDLE), released in v1.76.0.
- Neither was backported to grpc-go 1.72.x.
- kubernetes master picked up the fix incidentally via routine dependency maintenance (#136227, grpc v1.78.0; then #137906, v1.79.3), so 1.36 is fixed. release-1.35 (through v1.35.7) and release-1.34 still vendor grpc-go v1.72.2.

Potential root cause (from Claude): 

internal/transport/http2_client.go strands in-flight RPCs when a transport leaves service:

- Close(): calls t.onClose(...) first the subchannel immediately reports the transport dead and new RPCs move to a fresh transport — then waits for GOAWAY write, then blocks on <-t.readerDone with no deadline, and only after that errors the in-flight streams. If the dying connection goes mute (no FIN/RST reaches the reader), in-flight streams wait indefinitely.
- GracefulClose(): calls t.onClose(...) and then waits for active streams to drain with no deadline; in-flight streams are never errored at all.

So an RPC that lands on a transport just as it is being recycled is stranded on attempt 0: the etcd retry interceptor never sees the attempt finish, so it never retries, while every new RPC succeeds on the replacement transport. The etcd client defaults to WaitForReady(true), so nothing bounds the attempt client-side. The only recovery paths are the etcd client keepalive configured in storagebackend/factory/etcd3.go (30s ping / 10s timeout → ~40–86s) or the HTTP request's own context ending (server --request-timeout, or the caller disconnecting — which is what we observed).

Two things make first-requests-to-CRDs a reliable trigger window: per-CRD lazy storage creation churns subchannels exactly when the request is issued, and with ResilientWatchCacheInitialization a LIST arriving before the CRD's watch cache is ready delegates straight to etcd (cacher/delegator.go), putting the user request directly on the brand-new transport.

Caveat: the chain above is established from the logs plus reading the vendored code; we have not reproduced it with a patched grpc-go to bisect.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

Kubernetes: v1.35.6
etcd server v3.5.24,
</details>


### Cloud provider

<details>
GCP, our own test harness that runs API server only and Calico components 
</details>


### OS version

<details>

```console
Ubuntu 22.04
Kernel 6.8.0-1064 - the HWE/GCP kernel
```

</details>

items.body:
The e2e test framework has several patterns that cause flakiness, silent resource leaks, and hard-to-debug failures, especially in disruptive tests that restart API servers or control plane components. PR 137832 addresses these across 13 files (185 additions, 41 deletions), touching SIG api-machinery, apps, cloud-provider, network, node, storage, and testing.

Error suppression hides resource leaks. Across the test suite, cleanup code discards errors from Delete calls. In test/e2e/apimachinery/aggregator.go, the cleanupSampleAPIServer function has 10 such calls (APIService, Deployment, Secret, Service, ServiceAccount, RoleBinding, ClusterRoleBinding, ClusterRole) all silently swallowed. Same pattern in test/e2e/apimachinery/apply.go (4 deployments/pods), test/e2e/apps/rc.go (DeleteCollection), and test/e2e/apps/statefulset.go (ConfigMaps in defer blocks). When these fail, resources leak into subsequent tests with zero trace of what went wrong.

No retry on transient API server errors. GetControlPlaneNodes in test/e2e/framework/util.go calls Nodes().List() and immediately fails on any error. During disruptive tests (daemon restarts, etcd failure injection), the API server is expected to be briefly unreachable. The same issue exists in allNodesReady at test/e2e/framework/node/helper.go and RestartNodes at test/e2e/common/util.go. A transient connection refused or 503 kills the entire test instead of retrying. The fix introduces IsRetryableAPIError which checks for connection refused/reset, server timeout, 429, 503, 500, and unexpected server errors, plus a new WaitForControlPlaneNodes that wraps the listing in a polling loop with retry-on-transient logic.

Healthz returns 200 before daemon is ready. RestartDaemonConfig.waitUp in test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go considers the daemon ready when /healthz returns HTTP 200. After a kubelet restart, the health endpoint can report ok while kubelet is still recovering. Logs show errors, pods are not yet scheduled. The fix adds verifyDaemonReadiness which SSHes into the node and checks the last 20 lines of /var/log/kubelet.log for error patterns before declaring readiness.

Goroutines not gracefully stopped. In test/e2e/apps/daemon_restart.go, a cache.NewInformer controller is started with go controller.Run(backgroundCtx.Done()). The cleanup calls cancel() but does not wait for the controller goroutine to finish. The fix replaces this with a dedicated stopCh channel and DeferCleanup that closes the channel then sleeps 100ms to allow graceful shutdown.

PVC deletion races with pod references. DeleteAllStatefulSets in test/e2e/framework/statefulset/rest.go has a TODO comment about not checking whether pods still reference PVCs before deleting them. The current code deletes PVCs immediately, which can fail or leave orphaned PVs when pods are still running. The fix lists pods, checks volume references, and only deletes PVCs that are not in use, with foreground propagation.

Duplicated control plane filtering. GetControlPlaneNodes and WaitForControlPlaneNodes both contain the same node filtering logic (check for control-plane label and NoSchedule taint). The second commit extracts this into a shared filterControlPlaneNodes helper.

All changes are in e2e test code, no user-facing impact.

Related issues:
- 109600: prevent the Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred()) and ExpectNoError(err) anti-pattern in e2e tests (same category of error handling problems)
- 86253: sample-apiserver returns error instead of falling back to second Accept type (directly affects the aggregator.go test modified in this PR)
- 135285: GOAWAY are not handled gracefully in apiserver when aggregating (related network error handling)
- 105536: Orphaned pod found, but error not a directory occurred when trying to remove the volumes dir (related resource cleanup issue)

items.title: APF queueset can panic ("slice bounds out of range") and crash the apiserver when a queue holding a lingering request is removed after a DesiredNumQueues reduction

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

items.body:
### What happened?

In `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/util/flowcontrol/fairqueuing/queueset/queueset.go`, a request that has finished its main service but still occupies seats during its `AdditionalLatency` (a "lingering" request, e.g. a mutating request whose work estimate reserves seats for its watch fan-out) is removed from `requestsExecuting` immediately in `finishRequestLocked`, while releasing its seats and calling `removeQueueIfEmptyLocked` is deferred to an `EventAfterDuration` callback that fires `AdditionalLatency` later.

`removeQueueIfEmptyLocked` decides whether to drop an excess queue using:

```go
if len(qs.queues) > qs.qCfg.DesiredNumQueues &&
    r.queue.requestsWaiting.Length() == 0 &&
    r.queue.requestsExecuting.Len() == 0 {   // does not check seatsInUse
    qs.queues = removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes(qs.queues, r.queue.index)
    ...
}
```

It does not check `seatsInUse`. So if `DesiredNumQueues` has been reduced (excess queues draining by attrition) and a queue Q holds a lingering request `r` plus another request `s`, then when `s` finishes it sees Q as empty (0 waiting, 0 executing — `r` was already removed from the executing set) and removes Q, even though `r`'s seats still linger. `removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes` only fixes up the `index` field of the *kept* queues, so the removed Q keeps a now-stale `index`, and `r.queue` still points at it. When `r`'s lingering timer later fires, its deferred `removeQueueIfEmptyLocked(r)` calls `removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes(qs.queues, <stale index>)` a second time:

- if the stale index is out of range for the now-shorter slice, `queues[index+1:]` panics with `slice bounds out of range`;
- otherwise it removes a different, live queue, silently corrupting fairness/seat accounting and stranding that flow's requests.

The panic runs in the goroutine spawned by `eventclock.Real.EventAfterDuration` (`go func(){ t := <-ch; f(t) }()`), which has no `recover`, so it crashes the whole apiserver process.

### What did you expect to happen?

The queue should not be removed while a lingering request still holds seats in it, and it should never be removed twice.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Unit-level, with the queueset's fake event clock (test in `package queueset`):

1. Build a queuing queueset with `DesiredNumQueues: 3, HandSize: 1` and ample concurrency.
2. `StartRequest` two requests with the same hash (so they share queue index 2): `r` with `WorkEstimate{InitialSeats:1, FinalSeats:1, AdditionalLatency: time.Second}` (lingering) and `s` normal.
3. Reconfigure to `DesiredNumQueues: 1` (the three queues remain, draining by attrition).
4. `r.Finish(...)` then `s.Finish(...)`.
5. Advance the fake clock past `AdditionalLatency`.

Result on current master: `panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [3:2]` in `removeQueueAndUpdateIndexes`, from the lingering timer callback. (A regression test is attached; it panics before the fix and passes after.)


### Anything else we need to know?

Trigger requires an operator to reduce a PriorityLevelConfiguration's `queuing.queues` (so excess queues are draining) together with the right concurrent traffic and timing, so probability is low; but the consequence (apiserver panic, or silent fairness corruption) is severe, and it is reachable through supported configuration. This is a robustness bug on configuration change, not a security issue (no unprivileged trigger, no escalation).

Fix: add `&& r.queue.seatsInUse == 0` to the `removeQueueIfEmptyLocked` guard so a queue is not removed while a lingering request still holds its seats; the queue is then removed exactly once, by the lingering request's own deferred call after its seats are released.

### Kubernetes version

Current master (aa94f417962)

### Cloud provider

N/A (apiserver unit-level).

items.title: CRD with identical per-version selectableFields but differing per-version schemas is rejected due to internal hoisting

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

items.body:
### What happened?

Creating a multi-version `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` CRD that declares the **same** `selectableFields` on two served versions whose **schemas differ** is rejected by the apiserver:

```
The CustomResourceDefinition "widgets.example.com" is invalid:
spec.selectableFields: Invalid value: "": may only be set when validations.schema is included
```

The error is doubly confusing: the manifest sets only `spec.versions[*].selectableFields` (valid per the v1 API), yet the error references top-level `spec.selectableFields` — a field that does not exist in the v1 API the user submitted.

**Root cause (from reading the source):** `Convert_v1_CustomResourceDefinitionSpec_To_apiextensions_CustomResourceDefinitionSpec` (`staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/v1/conversion.go`) hoists each of the four per-version fields (`subresources`, `schema`, `additionalPrinterColumns`, `selectableFields`) to the internal top-level spec **independently**, whenever that field is identical across all versions. So with identical `selectableFields` but differing schemas:

- `selectableFields` **is** hoisted to internal `spec.SelectableFields` (and cleared per-version),
- `schema` is **not** hoisted (internal `spec.Validation` stays nil),

and internal validation then rejects the combination the conversion itself created (top-level `selectableFields` requires a top-level `validations.schema`). The user's input was never invalid; the independent hoisting manufactured the invalid internal state.

### What did you expect to happen?

Per-version `selectableFields` to be accepted on any served version, independent of whether the other versions' schemas are identical. KEP-4358 field selectors are declared per-version in v1; whether two versions happen to share a schema should not change the validity of identical selector declarations.

**Real-world impact:** any multi-version CRD mid-graduation — the standard pattern of serving two versions where the newer one drops deprecated fields — cannot offer the same field selector on both served versions. We hit this graduating a CRD whose new version removes two deprecated fields; controllers watching via field selector on the old version could not keep the selector when the new version was added. Workarounds: declare `selectableFields` on only one version (losing field selectors on the others), or keep the version schemas byte-identical (defeating the point of graduation).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply this CRD:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: widgets
    singular: widget
    kind: Widget
    listKind: WidgetList
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    selectableFields:
    - jsonPath: .spec.name
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              name: {type: string}
              extra: {type: string}   # <- v1-only field: schemas differ
  - name: v2
    served: true
    storage: false
    selectableFields:
    - jsonPath: .spec.name
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              name: {type: string}
```

→ rejected with the error above.

Control matrix (verified against kube-apiserver v1.35.0):

| per-version schemas | selectableFields | result |
|---|---|---|
| differ | on one version only | accepted |
| differ | identical on both | **rejected** |
| identical | identical on both | accepted (both hoist together) |

The identical-schemas row confirms the failure is the hoisting *interaction*, not the field declarations themselves.

### Anything else we need to know?

Possible fixes:

- Couple the hoisting: hoist `selectableFields` (and `additionalPrinterColumns`/`subresources`) only when `schema` is also hoisted; or
- Relax the spec validation to accept internal top-level `selectableFields` without a top-level schema when every version carries a schema.

Either preserves round-tripping while accepting the valid v1 input. Independent of the fix, the error message would benefit from mentioning that identical per-version declarations can trigger it, since `spec.selectableFields` is not settable in the v1 API.

/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
kube-apiserver v1.35.0 (reproduced via envtest / controller-runtime, direct API access).
The hoisting code cited above is unchanged in k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver v0.36.0.
```

</details>

### Cloud provider

None — local kube-apiserver (envtest).

</details>

items.title: CEL map-list concatenation preserves duplicate new keys from the right operand

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR lacks a `triage/foo` label and requires one.

items.body:
### What happened?

Schema-aware CEL map-list concatenation keeps duplicate new keys from the right operand instead of merging them.

`addToMapList` builds an index for the left operand, but does not add a key to that index when it appends the first new element from the right operand. A later element with the same key is therefore appended again.

For a map list keyed by `key1,key2`, if `x.mapList` contains two existing entries, this expression currently produces four entries and preserves both values `9` and `10`:

```cel
x.mapList + [
  {'key1': 'new', 'key2': 'key', 'value': 9},
  {'key1': 'new', 'key2': 'key', 'value': 10},
]
```

This breaks the merge-by-key semantics implemented for `x-kubernetes-list-type: map`. CEL policies that construct or inspect associative lists can observe the wrong size/value. Mutation expressions can also emit duplicate map keys, causing the admission request to be rejected instead of applying the later value.

### What did you expect to happen?

The first new key from the right operand should be appended and indexed. A later element with that key should overwrite it in place, so the example has one `new,key` entry with value `10`.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Add this case to `TestListAdd` in `staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/cel/common/values_test.go` using the existing `x.mapList` fixture:

```go
{
    name: "map list + literal list merges duplicate new keys",
    expression: "size(x.mapList + [{'key1': 'k1v9', 'key2': 'k2v9', 'value': 9}, {'key1': 'k1v9', 'key2': 'k2v9', 'value': 10}]) == 3 && (x.mapList + [{'key1': 'k1v9', 'key2': 'k2v9', 'value': 9}, {'key1': 'k1v9', 'key2': 'k2v9', 'value': 10}])[2].value == 10",
}
```

Then run:

```console
GOWORK=off go test ./pkg/cel/common -run TestListAdd -count=1
```

The case fails with `Expected true with typed values but got false` on current `master`.

### Anything else we need to know?

The behavior is in the map-list concatenation support merged by #140292. Updating `keyToIdx` immediately after appending a new key fixes the regression and makes the test pass.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

```console
master at 6720f0f96000abb82ad51d1177489b04188819d8
```

</details>

### Cloud provider

<details>

Not applicable; this is a schema-aware CEL evaluation bug.

</details>

### OS version

Not applicable.

### Install tools

Not applicable.

### Container runtime (CRI) and version (if applicable)

Not applicable.

items.body:
### What happened?

Creating a `StorageVersionMigration` for a resource, then removing that resource from the cluster (e.g. deleting the CRD) while the migration is still pending, makes the `kube-controller-manager` panic and enter `CrashLoopBackOff`.

The storage-version-migrator controller's `sync` dereferences a nil `*schema.GroupVersionResource`:

```
E0714 13:08:33 "Observed a panic" panic="runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference"
	k8s.io/kubernetes/pkg/controller/storageversionmigrator.(*SVMController).sync(...)
		pkg/controller/storageversionmigrator/storageversionmigrator.go:227
...
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [recovered, repanicked]
```

In `sync`, `resourceFor` returns `(nil, false, nil)` when the resource is not in the RESTMapper (this is the normal "unknown resource" return, not an error), and the following line logs `gvr.String()` on that nil pointer:

```go
gvr, exists, err := resourceFor(svmc.restMapper, toBeProcessedSVM.Spec.Resource)
if err != nil { return err }
if !exists {
    logger.V(4).Info("resource does not exist in our rest mapper", "gvr", gvr.String()) // gvr is nil -> panic
    ...
}
```

`GroupVersionResource.String()` has a value receiver, so calling it on a nil pointer dereferences it. The arguments of `logger.V(4).Info(...)` are evaluated unconditionally, so this happens regardless of the log verbosity. The panic crashes the whole controller-manager (all controllers stop) until the offending `StorageVersionMigration` is removed.

Note: the sibling function in the same package (`ResourceVersionController.sync` in `resourceversion.go`) handles the exact same `!exists` case without touching `gvr`, which is what makes this look like an oversight.

### What did you expect to happen?

The controller should handle a missing resource gracefully (it already intends to: it requeues for up to one minute, then marks the migration failed) without panicking or crashing the controller-manager.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

On a cluster with the `StorageVersionMigrator` feature enabled and the `storagemigration.k8s.io/v1beta1` API served:

```bash
# 1. A CRD (migrating a CRD to a new storage version is a documented use case)
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata: {name: widgets.example.com}
spec:
  group: example.com
  names: {plural: widgets, singular: widget, kind: Widget, listKind: WidgetList}
  scope: Namespaced
  versions: [{name: v1, served: true, storage: true, schema: {openAPIV3Schema: {type: object}}}]
YAML

# 2. Request a storage version migration for that resource
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: storagemigration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: StorageVersionMigration
metadata: {name: migrate-widgets}
spec: {resource: {group: example.com, resource: widgets}}
YAML

# 3. Delete the CRD (it leaves the RESTMapper) while the migration is pending
kubectl delete crd widgets.example.com
```

Within ~30-60s the kube-controller-manager panics and goes into CrashLoopBackOff:

```bash
kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l component=kube-controller-manager   # restartCount increasing, CrashLoopBackOff
kubectl -n kube-system logs <kcm-pod> --previous | grep -A2 "nil pointer"
```

Removing the `StorageVersionMigration` (`kubectl delete storageversionmigration migrate-widgets`) lets the controller-manager recover.

A unit-level reproduction (fake client, no cluster) is also available if you want it.

### Anything else we need to know?

Root cause is a single line (`gvr.String()` on a nil pointer). Trigger requires cluster-admin rights (StorageVersionMigration is cluster-scoped) plus the target resource disappearing from the RESTMapper, so this is not a privilege-escalation issue, but the crash takes down the entire controller-manager.

I have a fix ready (a one-line change: log the migration's `spec.resource` instead of the nil `gvr`) plus a regression test that panics without the fix and passes with it, and I'm happy to open a PR.

```console
Server Version: v1.36.1
```

items.body:
/kind bug
/sig api-machinery

### What happened?

`k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml.YAMLOrJSONDecoder` (via the underlying `YAMLReader`/`LineReader`) corrupts UTF-16 encoded input: a valid, BOM'd UTF-16 LE YAML document comes out of `YAMLReader.Read()` one byte longer than it went in — an odd-length UTF-16 stream — and the downstream yaml parser then fails with `yaml: incomplete UTF-16 character`. The error blames the user's file for being truncated when the file is actually valid; the truncation is introduced by the reader itself.

The yaml parser is not at fault: go-yaml is a libyaml port and handles BOM'd UTF-16 natively — `yaml.v2`, `yaml.v3` and `sigs.k8s.io/yaml` all parse the same bytes fine when handed the unmangled stream.

The corruption is in `LineReader.Read()`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/v0.36.2/pkg/util/yaml/decoder.go#L447-L461

`bufio.Reader.ReadLine()` (L456) splits at the raw `0x0a` byte — a UTF-8 assumption — and strips it, then `buffer.WriteByte('\n')` (L459) re-appends a *single-byte* UTF-8 newline. Mid-stream this happens to round-trip: each two-byte `0a 00` newline loses its `0a` to `ReadLine`, gains a fresh `0a` from `WriteByte`, and the orphaned `00` leads the next line, so the bytes reassemble in order. But at EOF the orphaned final `00` comes back as one more "line" and gets its own appended `0a`, so the stream grows by one byte and every subsequent UTF-16 code unit boundary is intact except the total length is now odd. A 314-byte document exits the reader as 315 bytes ending `... 0a 00 0a`.

This is byte-for-byte the encoding Windows PowerShell 5.1 produces with a plain `>` redirect, so "I wrote a manifest on Windows and the controller says my YAML is broken" is the practical failure mode.

### What did you expect to happen?

One of:

- BOM-detected UTF-16 input parses successfully. There is 10-year-old precedent for exactly this: kubectl has transcoded UTF-16 at the file-reading layer since 2016 (#39008), and still does — https://github.com/kubernetes/cli-runtime/blob/master/pkg/resource/visitor.go#L558-L561 wraps every file in `unicode.BOMOverride(unicode.UTF8.NewDecoder())` before the decoder sees it. That protection lives only in cli-runtime's `FileVisitor`; every other consumer of `YAMLOrJSONDecoder`/`YAMLReader` (controllers, operators, anything decoding user-supplied streams) is exposed.
- Or an early, explicit error ("unsupported encoding: UTF-16; convert to UTF-8") instead of silent corruption plus a misleading parser error.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Encode any valid manifest as UTF-16 LE with BOM (what PowerShell `echo ... > file.yaml` writes):

```console
$ { printf '\xff\xfe'; iconv -f UTF-8 -t UTF-16LE svc.yaml; } > svc-utf16.yaml
```

```go
package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"bytes"
	"fmt"
	"os"

	utilyaml "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/yaml"
)

func main() {
	data, _ := os.ReadFile("svc-utf16.yaml")

	var out map[string]interface{}
	err := utilyaml.NewYAMLOrJSONDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data), 4096).Decode(&out)
	fmt.Println("Decode err:", err)

	r := utilyaml.NewYAMLReader(bufio.NewReader(bytes.NewReader(data)))
	chunk, _ := r.Read()
	fmt.Printf("reader in: %d bytes, out: %d bytes\n", len(data), len(chunk))
}
```

Output (apimachinery v0.36.2):

```
Decode err: error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: incomplete UTF-16 character
reader in: 314 bytes, out: 315 bytes
```

The same file parses fine with `sigs.k8s.io/yaml.Unmarshal` directly, and with `kubectl apply -f` (thanks to the cli-runtime transcoder).

### Anything else we need to know?

Real-world sighting: this is the root cause of fluxcd/flux2#1126 (2021) — kustomize-controller validated user manifests through kustomize's legacy `kunstruct` factory, which delegates to `NewYAMLOrJSONDecoder`, and PowerShell-authored files failed with this exact error. Full RCA with byte traces: https://github.com/fluxcd/flux2/issues/1126#issuecomment-4967789882. Flux escaped by rewriting its generator, but the trap remains armed for any other consumer.

Verified present in v0.20.2 through v0.36.2; `LineReader` is unchanged on master.

Happy to send a PR. Two possible directions — transcode on BOM detection at `YAMLReader`/`YAMLOrJSONDecoder` entry (can be done with stdlib `unicode/utf16`, no new dependency, mirroring what cli-runtime does with `x/text`), or reject non-UTF-8 input early with a clear error. Whichever SIG API Machinery prefers.

### Kubernetes version

N/A — library bug in `k8s.io/apimachinery` (verified v0.20.2 → v0.36.2, master unchanged).

### Cloud provider

N/A

### OS version

N/A
